Caption: Image 1. The relief panel at Behistun. Darius (at left, facing right) stands on the fallen Gaumata; the captured rebel leaders stand roped at the neck before him, and the winged figure hovers above. Columns of cuneiform text surround the panel. The panel is carved high on the cliff face, far above the road.
Image 2. Detail: Darius raises one hand toward the winged figure and rests his foot on the prostrate Gaumata. Two attendants stand behind the king (only partly visible at left).
The Cyrus Cylinder, baked clay with Akkadian cuneiform, on display in the British Museum. Part of the surface is missing, and a large crack runs across the center.

Image 1. Northern wall of the east stairway: a procession of Persian and Median dignitaries. Figures in fluted headdresses and long robes alternate with figures in rounded caps and tunics; a stylized tree stands at left.

Image 2. Southern wall of the east stairway: a delegation usually identified as Lydians (from western Anatolia), bringing vessels, cups, bracelets, and a small chariot drawn by horses (at left). The first man is led by an usher at far left, outside this view.
Image 3. Southern wall of the east stairway: a delegation usually identified as Ionian Greeks, carrying folded textiles, skeins of wool, and objects that may be beehives or bowls.
Image 1. Augustus of Prima Porta, marble, height about 2.08 m. Vatican Museums, Rome.

Image 2. Breastplate detail (crop of Image 1). Center: a man in eastern dress (usually identified as a Parthian) hands a Roman standard topped by an eagle to a figure in Roman military dress. Above, a sky god spreads a canopy; the sun god’s chariot rises at upper left. Seated figures at the sides are usually read as conquered or client peoples. At the bottom, an earth goddess holds a horn of plenty.

Image 1. Qin bronze weight with inscribed edicts, displayed at the Qin Shihuang Mausoleum Museum, Lintong, Shaanxi. The characters are cut in small seal script, the standardized script promoted by the Qin.

Image 2. Early-20th-century ink rubbing of the First Emperor’s 221 B.C.E. edict on a Qin bronze standard weight (original weight in the Yūrinkan Museum, Kyoto). Read the columns from right to left, beginning at top right with 廿六年 (“twenty-sixth year”).
Image 1. Panorama of Pit 1, the largest pit, showing rows of standing infantry figures in earthen corridors. Earthen walls once supported a timber roof over each corridor.
Image 2. A kneeling archer figure (painted terracotta), displayed in the site museum. Kneeling archers of this type were found in Pit 2. The hands once held a real crossbow.
Image 3. Bronze chariot and team of four horses, about half life-size, found near the burial mound in 1980 and restored from many fragments. Qin Shihuang Mausoleum Museum.

Image 1. Leaf illustrating the chapter on the filial piety of high ministers and great officers (Chapter IV below), from the album Illustrations of the Classic of Filial Piety. Ink and colors on silk, Song dynasty (960–1279), National Palace Museum, Taipei. A seated personage in a pavilion is attended by standing officials, while a man in red bows low in the courtyard. The identification of the figures is the editor’s reading of the scene, not the museum’s caption.

Image 2. Leaf illustrating the chapter on the filial piety of the common people (Chapter VI below), from the same album. Two elders sit on a mat under a thatched roof; a kneeling attendant offers a bowl, and two standing women (one holding a bowl, one beside a child) wait on them; outside the fence a man plows with an ox and another carries a hoe. How the figures are related is the viewer’s inference from the painter’s conventions.

Image 1. The Great Stupa (Stupa 1) at Sanchi, Madhya Pradesh, India, with the eastern gateway and the stone railing. Brick and sandstone; core 3rd century B.C.E., enlarged and enclosed later. Photograph: Rohit Sharma, 2023.

Image 2. Eastern gateway, Stupa 1: the departure from Kapilavastu. Sandstone relief, about the 1st century B.C.E.–1st century C.E. A crowded scene of men, horses, and attendants beside the balconies of a city (black-and-white photograph); the identification as the departure of Prince Siddhartha follows the photographer’s caption. Photograph: Anandajoti Bhikkhu, 2017.

Image 3. Northern gateway, Stupa 1: the Buddha’s descent at Sankissa. Sandstone relief, about the 1st century B.C.E.–1st century C.E. A ladder and an empty seat beneath a tree stand for the Buddha; worshippers with joined hands stand at each side. Photograph: Anandajoti Bhikkhu, 2017.

Data: Hodell, Curtis, and Brenner, as archived by NOAA. There are 48 dated samples in this window, unevenly spaced; Physocypria values are missing for 12 of them (including every sample from 789 to 891) and Pyrgophorus for one (871), so the lines are broken there. The units are per mil, as in the NOAA file, which does not state the reference standard.
